title: "TMUA Preparation"

Everything is on this page. Papers, lessons, and the Paper 2 toolkit, in three tables.

::: {.callout-tip}
## The test in one box

Two papers, **75 minutes each, taken back to back**, **20 multiple-choice questions** per paper —
**3 min 45 s per question**. **No calculator. No formula booklet. No penalty for a wrong answer**, so
never leave a blank. One overall score from **1.0 to 9.0**; a typical candidate scores about **4.5**,
and roughly **10% score above 7.0**.

**Paper 1 — Applications of Mathematical Knowledge.** AS-level pure content, but engineered so the
direct route is too slow. You are being tested on finding the *shorter* route.
**Paper 2 — Mathematical Reasoning.** Logic, proof, and finding the error in a false proof. Assumes
everything in Paper 1 *plus* material no A-Level course teaches.

Full detail: **[The Test](about/format.qmd)** — format, scoring, what changed in 2024, how to prepare.
:::

**Do not attempt these until the toolkit below is covered.** Paper 2 assumes Paper 1 *and* Section 2
(logic and proof), which is not taught in any A-Level course. Sitting a Paper 2 cold mostly teaches
frustration.

::: {.callout-note}
## This archive is complete and closed

2023 was the last paper-based sitting. Since 2024 the TMUA has been computer-based at Pearson VUE and
**no further papers are published**, so these nine sittings — 360 questions — are all there is.
Spend them deliberately: keep the three most recent unseen for timed mocks near the test date, and
treat 2019–2023 as the best model of what the live test now asks.
:::

## Paper 2 Toolkit — Logic and Proof

The part that is **not in the A-Level syllabus**. A student can be excellent at A-Level Maths and still
score badly on Paper 2, simply because nobody ever told them what *"A only if B"* means. Work through
these in order — each is built on the one before.

| | Session | Spec |
|---|---|---|
| **S1** | **[Statement forms — if, only if, if and only if](toolkit/s01_statement_forms.qmd)** | Arg1 |
| S2 | Converse and contrapositive | Arg1 |
| S3 | Necessary and sufficient | Arg2 |
| S4 | Quantifiers and negation | Arg3, Arg4 |
| S5 | Proof methods — direct, cases, contradiction, counterexample | Prf1 |
| S6 | Scrambled proofs | Prf4 |
| S7 | Spot the error | Err1, Err2 |

*(S2–S7 not written yet. Toolkit overview: **[Paper 2 Toolkit](toolkit/index.qmd)**.)*

| [Content Specification](https://uat-wp.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/03165619/TMUA_Content_Specification.pdf) | The syllabus, for the October 2026 and January 2027 sittings. Section 1 = maths (both papers), Section 2 = logic and proof (Paper 2 only) |
| [Notes on Mathematics](https://uat-wp.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/30103537/Notes_on_Mathematics_-for_TMUA_and_ESAT_M2.pdf) | 159 pages, MM1–MM8, mapped one-to-one onto Section 1. The setters' own commentary on what each spec line means |

| [Pearson VUE practice tests](https://www.pearsonvue.com/us/en/uatuk.html) | The on-screen interface. Sit one, for the format rather than the maths |
